fields.as_of: the last close the file describes (New York trading day)
fields.market: spy (close), spy_trend (above / below its 100-day average), spy_vs_100d (0.031 = 3.1% above), vix (close), vix_band (low under 15, mid 15 to 25, high over 25)
fields.week: start: this week's signal day (its first trading day; new picks happen only then), next_start: the next one as far as the calendar knows
fields.lists: the yearly rule lists in force: at (its first signal day), saved (true: the official list on the reports branch; false: chosen by this run the same way), buys and shorts kept
fields.rules: every kept rule of the lists in force, by name: side, h (trading days held), pick (top: the score's rank among all scored stocks, or level: the score itself) with value, trend, vix, sector, extra (see pulse.search), and n, hit, mean (its numbers when the list was chosen, against SPY) and record (its signals as counted here)
fields.record: the signals since January 2025, the app's way: long (every buy, hit = made money), short (hit = did worse than SPY), cautious (the buys among long first picked while SPY was under its 100-day average); each with n closed, hit, avg and median result (0.031 = 3.1%), days held, open, open_now (mean result so far of the open ones), and hit_other / avg_other on the other measure (buys against SPY, shorts on their own price)
fields.signals: open: every signal that runs at the close (ticker, side, rule, first pick day, last_pick (the last week that picked it; each pick moves the exit out), entry, planned exit (exit), held (trading days held so far), days (in all), weeks picked, cautious, new: first picked this week, picked_this_week, ret: its result so far from its side, vs_spy so far, score now); closed: those that exited in the last 30 trading days with their final ret, vs_spy and hit
fields.stocks: every scored stock at the close: t, name, sector, industry, score (0 to 100), base (before seasonality), the six parts (momentum, fundamentals, analysts, smart_money, attention, seasonality; null when missing), parts (how many have a value), rank (1 = highest score), d1 and d5 (the score's change over 1 and 5 trading days), season (long / short / null: a seasonal window counts today), vol and size (terciles, 1 = calmest / smallest), trend (the score on each of the last 30 trading days, oldest first, null when missing), index (sp500, or ndx for a Nasdaq-100 name outside the S&P 500). The ndx names (Ran, 2026-11-21) have a score and no signals, placed among the S&P 500 members of each day as if each alone had joined them, so they move no member's score, rank or signal; their rank is null, and vol and size are their terciles among the members
fields.etfs: every scored equity ETF (catalog v4: a score and no signals, Ran 2026-11-18), ranked among the ETFs: t, name, group, etf (true), score, base, the parts momentum, positioning and seasonality, parts, rank, d1, d5, season, close, as_of (its last close) and trend, as for stocks
